gold: Saturday night retinopathy with orbital compression syndrome

selector.rationale: High intraocular pressure and corneal haze support Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma, while tense eyelid edema and chemosis also point towards this diagnosis

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: Delayed choroidal and retinal arterial filling could be present, but other findings like high intraocular pressure and corneal haze are more indicative of Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma

rejected.label: Toxic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: Lack of direct evidence linking buprenorphine/naloxone to toxic optic neuropathy in this context

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: Elevated creatine kinase level suggests rhabdomyolysis, but it does not directly explain the ocular findings

rejected.label: Compressive optic neuropathy
rejected.why: While some findings could suggest compressive optic neuropathy, the presence of high intraocular pressure and other signs point more strongly towards Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
